title: Higgsfield vs an Agency for 3D Character Ads: Which to Pick
summary: Higgsfield is software you run yourself, while an agency delivers finished 3D character ads. Compare control, timing, prices and Meta ad rules.
body_markdown:
## Other agencies, and what each one publishes


Vidico's animation service page says it produces 2D animation, 3D animation and motion graphics end to end, including character animation, voiceover and sound design. As of October 2026, it lists monthly plans from around $5,000 with video, design and animation in one flat fee, and says most B2B explainers cost $5,000 to $12,000 per minute. Turnaround is not published, so get it in writing. The page is written for B2B and SaaS teams, so check whether it takes direct-response Meta work before you brief it.


B2W's animated commercial page lists fixed-fee packages from $2,400 for a 60-second video, with script, voiceover and sound design included. Vertical 9:16 and social cuts come with each project, and two rounds of revisions are included at the script, storyboard and animation stages. Most projects take 4 to 6 weeks from brief to final file, or 2 to 3 weeks with a rush fee. Its page names B2B brands, tech startups and cause campaigns, so confirm that it takes consumer direct-response work.


Biddyco makes motion graphics ads by hand, plus hybrids that layer animation, kinetic type and brand design over creator footage. Its process runs from scripts and storyboards to animation in After Effects, with a US-based motion team. Its Meta page says finished files arrive every two to four weeks depending on the plan, and it does not describe running campaigns, so confirm who buys the media before you brief it.


## What a 3D character ad needs that a UGC ad does not


A 3D character ad is judged in the first seconds of a feed, so the format rules matter as much as the animation. Meta's[Reels ads page](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/facebook-instagram-reels-ads) describes 9:16 vertical video, says Reels default to sound on, and recommends keeping key messages inside the safe zone. Build the character and any on-screen text for that frame from the first storyboard, not as a crop at the end.


Length is the next constraint. Meta's[video ad format page](https://www.facebook.com/business/ads/video-ad-format) says in-stream video can run from 5 seconds to 10 minutes but generally recommends a 15-second maximum. A character story with a long setup should be cut into short pieces that each make one point.


Labels and responsibility come next. Meta says it labels ads created or significantly edited with its own generative AI features when they add a photorealistic AI-generated person. It also says it will detect ads made or edited with third-party AI tools and show an "AI info" label in About this ad, although its[transparency post](https://about.fb.com/news/2025/02/gen-ai-transparency-metas-ads-products/) does not say that detection is live. A stylized character may sit outside the photorealistic rule, so ask each provider which tools touched each file. Meta's[Ad Creative Generative AI Terms](https://www.facebook.com/legal/terms/ad_creative_generative_ai_terms) make the advertiser solely responsible for checking the accuracy of output from Meta's tools, and that standard fits any AI animation.


Character ownership is the cost most buyers miss. The character model, rig and source files are the assets you will reuse for the next campaign, so the contract should name the owner and say whether you can use them after the engagement ends. Do not rely on a promise made on a sales call.


## How to run a fair test before you choose


Write one brief and send it on the same day to your own editor and to each provider you are considering. Include the product, one claim you can prove, the character spec (age, look, wardrobe and props) and the vertical length you need. Ask each side for a first draft by a set date, along with the number of revision rounds included.


Score the drafts on four things: usable seconds, the number of rounds needed to approve, whether the character stays consistent across cuts, and who fixes a claim that is wrong. Divide each route's total cost by the ads that pass your review, not by the number of generations or renders.


Judge the ads only after Meta's learning phase. Meta's[help page on the learning phase](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/112167992830700) says an ad set usually leaves learning after about 50 results in the week after its last significant edit, so an ad judged after two days, or edited every morning, tells you very little. Our[3D animated video ads guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/3d-animated-video-ads) covers the creative side, our[comparison of AI tools and hired teams for 3D characters](https://knowlify.com/articles/3d-character-ads-ai-tools-or-hire-someone) goes deeper on rights and consistency, and our[guide on whether animated ads work on Meta](https://knowlify.com/articles/do-animated-ads-work-on-meta) covers what the test should prove.


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify, our top pick, makes 3D and stylized character animation ads as a done-for-you service, with a person checking every ad and optional Meta management.
- Higgsfield is studio software. Changing a video means generating it again, so budget for regenerations and review time.
- Published agency terms vary: Vidico from around $5,000 a month, B2W from $2,400 for a 60-second commercial, and Biddyco for brands spending $100k or more a month on Meta.
- Ask every provider who holds the character model, rig and source files, and whether you can reuse them.
- Judge both routes on cost per approved ad, after Meta's learning phase.


## FAQ


### What is the best option for 3D character ads?


Knowlify, our top pick, is the strongest fit when you want finished 3D and stylized character animation with a person checking every ad and no software to run. Get written quotes from at least two providers on the same brief before you choose. Knowlify starts at $5,000 a month, so compare it against other quotes on the same list of finished ads.


### Can Higgsfield make 3D character ads without a designer?


Its public pages list product, UGC and presenter modes, plus a CGI product commercial with no people, but they do not describe a 3D character pipeline. Test it with your own character brief and count the regenerations, because each change generates the video again. Judge the result by the approved ad, not the first output.


### Who owns the character after the campaign?


Ask in writing before the work starts, and get the answer into the contract. If you generate the character yourself in Higgsfield, check its Terms of Use for what it allows in paid campaigns. If an agency builds it, ask whether you receive the model and source files or only the finished videos.


### Do AI-animated ads need a label on Meta?


Meta labels ads created or significantly edited with its own generative AI tools when they add a photorealistic AI-generated person. It also says it will detect ads made or edited with third-party AI tools and show an "AI info" label, although its post does not say that detection is live. Ask providers which tools touched each file, so you can answer any label question quickly.


### How long does a 3D character ad take?


B2W's animated commercial page says most projects take 4 to 6 weeks from brief to final file, or 2 to 3 weeks with a rush fee. Biddyco says finished files arrive every two to four weeks, depending on the plan. Knowlify's first batch lands on day five, so ask each provider for its timeline in writing, including when the clock starts.
